slides.title: SELECT can't find *customer 1000*?
slides.voiceover: Your SELECT can't find customer one thousand? It's right there in the table. The culprit is leading zeros.
slides.spoken: Your SELECT can't find customer 1000? It's right there in the table. The culprit is leading zeros.

slides.label: THE PROBLEM
slides.heading: Typed *1000*, got *0 rows*
slides.title: ZCUSTOMER_NAME
slides.voiceover: Here's the problem. You search for one thousand. But KNA1 stores it with leading zeros, ten digits long. Result: zero rows.
slides.spoken: Here's the problem. You search for 1000. But KNA1 stores it with leading zeros, 10 digits long. Result: 0 rows.

slides.label: WHY
slides.heading: The *ALPHA* routine
slides.body: The KUNNR domain uses conversion routine ALPHA. Screens add the zeros for you. Your code doesn't.
slides.voiceover: Why? The KUNNR domain uses the ALPHA conversion routine. On screens, SAP adds the zeros for you. In your code, it doesn't.
slides.spoken: Why? The KUNNR domain uses the ALPHA conversion routine. On screens, SAP adds the zeros for you. In your code, it doesn't.

slides.heading: The fix: *ALPHA = IN*
slides.code:
DATA lv_kunnr TYPE kunnr VALUE '1000'.
lv_kunnr = |{ lv_kunnr ALPHA = IN }|.
SELECT SINGLE name1 FROM kna1
  WHERE kunnr = @lv_kunnr
  INTO @DATA(lv_name).
slides.voiceover: The fix is one line. A string template with ALPHA equals IN adds the zeros. Then run the SELECT.
slides.spoken: The fix is one line. A string template with ALPHA equals IN adds the zeros. Then run the SELECT.

slides.label: RESULT
slides.heading: Now it *finds it*
slides.title: ZCUSTOMER_NAME
slides.voiceover: Now the value has its zeros. The SELECT finds one row. ACME Limited. Done.
slides.spoken: Now the value has its zeros. The SELECT finds 1 row. ACME Limited. Done.

slides.label: REMEMBER
slides.heading: *Convert first*, then select
slides.body: ALPHA key fields need their leading zeros in code: ALPHA = IN before the WHERE.
slides.voiceover: Takeaway: convert the value first. Then select.
slides.spoken: Takeaway: convert the value first. Then select.

SAP ABAP leading zeros bug: the ALPHA conversion routine.

1. KNA1 stores KUNNR as 0000001000, not 1000
2. Screens add the zeros for you, your code doesn't
3. Fix: |{ lv_kunnr ALPHA = IN }| (or CONVERSION_EXIT_ALPHA_INPUT)
4. Then run the SELECT

slides.title: One change, *ten broken tables*?
slides.voiceover: Stop breaking ten tables with one change. Last time we learned documentation. Now, the key rules.
slides.spoken: Stop breaking ten tables with one change. Last time we learned documentation. Now, the key rules.

slides.heading: Four *key rules*
slides.voiceover: Here are four rules. One domain can carry many data elements. Labels are stored per logon language. Changes hit every table that uses it. Programs should type the data element.
slides.spoken: Here are four rules. One domain can carry many data elements. Labels are stored per logon language. Changes hit every table that uses it. Programs should type the data element.

slides.label: EXAMPLE
slides.heading: One domain *KUNNR*, three meanings
slides.title: Domain KUNNR: data elements
slides.voiceover: Here's an example. The KUNNR domain sits under many data elements. Customer. Sold to party. Ship to party. Same shape, different meaning.
slides.spoken: Here's an example. The KUNNR domain sits under many data elements. Customer. Sold to party. Ship to party. Same shape, different meaning.

slides.label: CHANGES
slides.heading: Check the *Where-Used List*
slides.body: A change to a data element reaches every table and program that uses it. Look before you change.
slides.voiceover: Before you change a data element, open the Where-Used List. Every table and program in it gets the change.
slides.spoken: Before you change a data element, open the Where-Used List. Every table and program in it gets the change.

slides.label: IN PROGRAMS
slides.heading: Programs *TYPE it*
slides.voiceover: In programs, don't use a plain ten character field. It gets no F1 and no F4. Type it with the data element, like KUNNR. Then F1 and F4 come along.
slides.spoken: In programs, don't use a plain ten character field. It gets no F1 and no F4. Type it with the data element, like KUNNR. Then F1 and F4 come along.

slides.label: REMEMBER
slides.heading: Domain = *shape*, data element = *meaning*
slides.body: Many data elements can share one domain. Always TYPE the data element.
slides.voiceover: Takeaway: the domain gives the shape. The data element gives the meaning.
slides.spoken: Takeaway: the domain gives the shape. The data element gives the meaning.
